title: SimBench-BW nvbit_drop_rate_exceeded sidecar
description: Sidecar emitted when the NVBit-traced run's producer-side drop counters indicate the captured trace is missing more than the declared fraction of expected records. Member of the trace-budget typed-reason family declared in tools/cloud/trace_budgets.py NVBIT_DROP_RATE_EXCEEDED_SIDECAR; pinned in the original-plan exclusion-taxonomy list. The producer-side drop-counter sources enumerated by the per-source counts below are: (1) NVBit channel overflow (the producer-side communication channel between the injected tracer and the consumer ran out of capacity), (2) ring-buffer loss (the per-warp ring buffer wrapped before the consumer could drain it), (3) decoder gaps (the consumer-side decoder skipped records it could not parse), (4) expected-record mismatch (the count of records the producer declared it would emit minus the count the consumer admitted). Each source is reported individually so the downstream model can attribute drop-rate to root cause; the schema requires all four counter fields so a future regression that drops a source without updating the schema fails the C-AC-C parity scanner.

schema_version.description: Sidecar schema major version. Pinned to 1; a deliberate schema bump must update both this constant and consumers in lockstep.

shape_point.description: Trace shape point name (from shapes/<slug>.toml) whose run crossed the drop-rate budget.

max_drop_rate.description: Declared maximum drop rate as a fraction in [0, 1]. A row's value of 0.01 means up to 1% of expected records may be dropped before the sidecar is required.

actual_drop_rate.description: Observed drop rate computed as 1 - admitted_record_count / max(1, expected_record_count). Strictly greater than 0; a value of 0 means no records were dropped and no sidecar should have been emitted.

expected_record_count.description: Total number of records the producer declared it would emit for this run. Sourced from the producer-side instrumentation count (one tick per warp memory instruction, threadblock-scope kernel record, etc.).

admitted_record_count.description: Total number of records the consumer admitted after schema and contract validation.

channel_overflow_dropped.description: Drop counter source (1 of 4): records lost because the producer-side communication channel between the injected tracer and the consumer ran out of capacity.

ring_buffer_loss_dropped.description: Drop counter source (2 of 4): records lost because the per-warp ring buffer wrapped before the consumer could drain it.

decoder_gap_dropped.description: Drop counter source (3 of 4): records the consumer-side decoder skipped because it could not parse them (typed-exclusion routing applies separately to records it could parse but rejected on contract grounds).

expected_record_mismatch_dropped.description: Drop counter source (4 of 4): the residual count when expected_record_count - admitted_record_count exceeds the sum of the other three named drop sources. A non-zero value here indicates an unattributed drop and should be treated as a reproducibility-blocking discrepancy.

trace_budgets_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical trace_budgets.toml at the time the run was admitted.
